endpoints.summary: Run unconditional generation. Returns a JobInfo; poll until completed.
endpoints.description: Run unconditional generation. Returns a JobInfo; poll until completed.

request_fields.name: n_mols
request_fields.description: Number of molecules to generate. Batched sampling; runtime scales linearly in ceil(n_mols / max_batch_size) forward passes.

request_fields.name: n_timesteps
request_fields.description: Number of Euler integration steps. 250 is the paper sweet spot; 100 already usable at slightly lower PB-Valid rate.

request_fields.name: n_atoms_per_mol
request_fields.description: If set, every molecule has exactly this many atoms. Default (null) samples atom counts from the training distribution per molecule — recommended.

request_fields.name: model_variant
request_fields.description: Which trained model to use. See flowmol3 wiki for the 3 primary + 19 ablation variants. `flowmol3` is the paper SOTA (default). Only pre-staged variants on NAS are usable — check /healthz/detail.staged_variants.

request_fields.name: seed
request_fields.description: pytorch-lightning `seed_everything`; null → framework fills a random seed and records it in JobInfo.input_params.
request_fields.default_note: random seed selected by the tool at runtime

request_fields.name: stochasticity
request_fields.description: CTMC sampling stochasticity η_t. Applies to `fm3_*` CTMC-parameterised variants (all of them). Null → upstream config default.

request_fields.name: hc_thresh
request_fields.description: High-confidence threshold for CTMC purity sampling. Null → upstream config default.

request_fields.name: max_batch_size
request_fields.description: Sampling batch size cap. n_mols > max_batch_size splits into ceil(n_mols / max_batch_size) forward passes.

examples.notes: Smallest useful call. Returns a JobInfo; poll /api/jobs/<id> until completed, then GET /api/jobs/<id>/file/molecules.sdf.

examples.title: fast smoke (10 mols, 100 steps)
examples.notes: Roughly 5-10 s on T4; useful for CI / warm-up.

examples.notes: Pins every generated molecule to exactly N atoms.

examples.title: FC async task mode (single 202 + blocking compute)
examples.curl: curl -X POST $URL/api/tasks/generate -H 'X-Fc-Invocation-Type: Async' -H 'X-Bioagent-Job-Id: my-job-001' -F n_mols=100 -F n_timesteps=250
examples.notes: Returns 202 immediately; FC keeps the instance alive until sampling completes. Preferred production entry.

job_lifecycle.poll_recommendation: Poll the status endpoint every 5–120 s until status ∈ {'completed', 'failed'}. On failure, JobInfo.error_summary holds a one-line exception summary and error_tail holds the trailing ~4 KB of the subprocess log — usually enough for triage without a separate /log fetch.
job_lifecycle.restart_semantics: Jobs survive process and FC instance restarts via a `job.json` sidecar in each job directory. Jobs that were RUNNING at the moment of restart are downgraded to FAILED with failure_kind='interrupted'.

nas_layout.cross_instance_consistency: When multiple FC instances mount the same NAS at jobs_base_dir, all of them can see each other's jobs via read-through cache on GET. Writes (create/update) only happen on the instance that owns the subprocess.
nas_layout.cross_service_sharing: Other bioagent services mounted on the same NAS can read this service's output files directly by path, avoiding HTTP round-trips. Example: another service does `Path('/data/rfantibody_jobs/<id>/output/file.qv').read_bytes()`.

model.name: FlowMol3
model.task: unconditional 3D de novo small-molecule generation (flow matching)

tool_outputs.generate: output/molecules.sdf — up to n_mols valid 3D molecules (SDF, kekulize=False). Actual count ≤ n_mols since unbuildable graphs are skipped. output/sampling_stats.json reports n_written vs n_requested.

config_tips.n_mols: 100 is a good sweet spot; batched sampling scales sublinearly.
config_tips.n_timesteps: 250 is paper SOTA; drop to 100 for quick smoke checks (small %PB-Valid loss).
config_tips.model_variant: Start with flowmol3 (paper SOTA). Ablation variants are for research; pre-stage them on NAS first.
